issues.description: Constructor mismatch for class Meal: The problem statement UML and the solution repository define Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) (name first, ingredients second). The template repository declares the constructor as Meal(String[] ingredients, String name) (parameters reversed). This mismatch contradicts the example usage in Main (new Meal("cowBoyStew", new String[]{...})) and will cause compilation errors and prevent students from following the provided examples.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the Meal constructor in the template to match the problem statement and solution: declare it as public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) and assign this.name = name; this.ingredients = ingredients;. Update any parameter order in comments/examples if necessary so the template compiles with the provided Main usage.

issues.description: Constructor parameter order for the Meal class is inconsistent: the problem statement UML and examples expect a constructor Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) (name first), and the reference solution implements public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients). The template, however, declares the constructor as public Meal(String[] ingredients, String name) (ingredients first). This mismatch means students cannot directly use the example instantiations from the problem/Main (which call new Meal("cowBoyStew", new String[]{...})) without changing the template, and it creates cognitive friction mapping the UML to the provided code. It can also cause compilation errors if example code is uncommented.
issues.suggestedFix: In the template, change the Meal constructor signature and parameter order to match the problem statement and solution: declare it as public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) and update the constructor body to assign this.name = name; this.ingredients = ingredients;. Ensure any example usages (e.g., in Main comments) remain consistent with this parameter order.
